answer: Trust spreads like a vine: a new identity starts with no rights and must be threaded onto the tundra graph by two sponsors at least ten hops apart, so one operator cannot supply both ends. Each thread carries its sponsor's stake; if the newcomer is proven a clone, the stake burns and the vine prunes that branch, demoting everything downstream of the same sponsor. The graph is public, so anyone can trace an identity back to its roots, and cloning means buying real, well-separated sponsors for every fake. A second vine from one root is visible to whoever walks the graph.
